Create a stateless RNG key

Source: R/key.R
rng_key.Rd

rng_key() creates immutable keys for the stateless generators in this package. A key vector is an opaque S3 object with one key per row; pass it to rng_fold() and the rng_*() samplers, but do not rely on its internal integer representation.

Usage

rng_key(seed, n = 1L, engine = c("xoshiro256pp", "philox4x64", "threefry4x64"))

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
length(x)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
x[i, ..., drop = FALSE]

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
x[i, ...] <- value

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
x[[i, ...]] <- value

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
as.list(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
rep(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
duplicated(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
unique(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
xtfrm(x)

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
x[[i, ...]]

# S3 method for class 'rng_key'
c(..., recursive = FALSE)

Arguments

seed

A single non-negative whole number.

n

A single non-negative whole number: how many keys to create.

engine

The engine. All three give the same guarantees: a value is a pure function of the key and the draw index, the same key gives the same values on every platform and thread count, and draw i does not depend on n. They differ in speed and in the stream they produce.

  • "xoshiro256pp" (default) – the fastest of the three, and faster than dqrng and RcppZiggurat on one thread (x86_64 and Apple Silicon; vignette("performance", package = "zurand") has the numbers). Philox derives a fresh 256-bit xoshiro256++ state for each 512-value chunk, then a cheap recurrence produces the chunk, so a chunk depends only on the key and its index. Reaching an arbitrary index costs at most 511 recurrence steps. Audited with PractRand to 1 TB, including interleaved streams of sibling and folded keys.

  • "philox4x64" – Philox4x64-10 from Random123, counter-based: each value is computed directly from its position.

  • "threefry4x64" – Threefry4x64-13 from Random123, counter-based; close to Philox in speed.

A key records its engine, so a key made with one never produces the other's values. Changing engine changes every number you get.

x

An rng_key.

...

Unused.

i

Integer or logical index selecting keys. Missing values, fractional numbers, infinities and positions beyond the key vector are an error: R would turn such an index into a key of missing words, the same invented key whatever vector it came from, so unrelated subsets would silently share one stream.

drop

Ignored; key subsetting always preserves the rng_key class.

value

Not used: keys are immutable, so assigning into a key vector is an error. Without these methods R would write the value into individual key words, silently producing different keys.

incomparables

Passed to duplicated().

recursive

Ignored. Included for compatibility with c().

Value

An object of class rng_key containing n keys.

Details

The samplers in this package never read or update .Random.seed. Calling a sampler twice with the same key and arguments returns the same values.

Key vectors

A key vector behaves like a vector of opaque keys: length(), [, [[, c(), rev(), rep(), unique(), duplicated() and as.list() work key by key and keep the engine and stream version, so lapply(keys, f), Map() and the parallel map functions hand each task one key. A key vector takes one index, as a vector does: keys[1, 2] and keys[, 1] are an error, not a view of the words inside. c() dispatches on its first argument, so combine key vectors with a key first: c(NULL, key) returns the bare integer words, not keys, while c(key, NULL) drops the NULL as c() does for any vector. Keys are immutable: assigning into a key vector is an error, and so is sorting one, since keys have no order; compare keys with identical().

Stream version

A key also records the version of the stream definition it was made under, as attr(key, "stream"); every key made by this version of zurand is stream 1L. If a defect in a stream is ever found after release, the fix becomes a new stream version for new keys, and existing keys – including saved ones – keep producing exactly the values they always did. A key saved before the attribute existed is treated as stream 1. A key from a newer stream than this version of zurand implements is an error rather than a silent reinterpretation.

Examples

key <- rng_key(42L)
keys <- rng_key(42L, n = 4L)
key
#> <rng_key> rng_key[2feb6e95bdd73226b266f10328efe333]
